assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski equality are exact, model-independent results that extend thermodynamics to small, driven, far-from-equilibrium systems. They give the second law a precise stochastic meaning at the level of single trajectories. This is the kind of simple, general mechanism that carries across molecular biophysics, colloids, nanoscale engines and information thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: Evans, Cohen and Morriss (1993) and Evans and Searles gave the first fluctuation theorem, Jarzynski (1997) the nonequilibrium work relation, Crooks (1999) the detailed fluctuation relation, and Seifert the framework of stochastic thermodynamics. Jarzynski, Evans and Seifert cover the origin, the best-known equality and the general framework. Crooks, and Cohen, Morriss and Searles outside the supplied names, have strong claims, so the three-person limit forces a hard cut.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed in RNA/DNA pulling experiments, colloidal and optical-trap systems, and single-electron devices. Theory is rigorous and stable, and thirty years have passed, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority among Evans, Jarzynski, Crooks and Seifert is genuinely contested, and I am recalling the history from memory rather than verifying it.
Whether the committee sees this as fundamental physics or as a broad theoretical framework with few single decisive experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KTHNY theory of two-dimensional melting, with a hexatic phase between solid and liquid driven by sequential unbinding of dislocations and disclinations, is a clean, universal and rigorously analysed mechanism. It applies to colloids, liquid crystals, films, vortex lattices and electrons. It extends the 2016 recognition of topological defects and phase transitions to a distinct and substantial body of theory.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson (1978) and Young (1979) developed the dislocation-mediated melting theory, building on Kosterlitz-Thouless. Kosterlitz and Thouless were already honoured in 2016, so the three named people fit a fair configuration. Young's role is slightly more derivative than the other two.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation from colloidal experiments, simulations (including the debated first-order versus continuous nature of the liquid-hexatic transition in some systems) and many later realisations. Very mature, and arguably late relative to the 2016 prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges that the 2016 prize already covered the essential idea.
System-dependent details, such as a first-order liquid-hexatic transition in some simulated systems, mean the confirmation is not uniform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a major field in which band topology gives robust edge and surface states. The theory is clear and general, and it was quickly confirmed experimentally. The impact extends to spintronics, photonics, Majorana physics and the classification of matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele (2005) proposed the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall state in graphene, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe, and Molenkamp's group observed it in 2007. Fu and Kane, Moore and Balents, and Hasan's ARPES work cover the three-dimensional case. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not among the supplied names, which leaves attribution unfair or incomplete. Kane, Mele and Molenkamp are the best supportable subset.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently many times, and the interpretation is stable. The delay since 2005-2007 is appropriate, and the prize would be timely.
uncertainties: Omission of Zhang (deceased) and Bernevig/Hughes from this candidate's credited names, and the separate claims of 3D topological insulators (Hasan), make the configuration contentious.
Overlap with candidates B009 and B023 on the same field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase show that gauge potentials and geometric phases have physical consequences. They reshaped understanding of quantum mechanics and recur throughout condensed matter, optics, molecular physics and topological matter. As a foundational result that already contained much of what followed, it is the sort of idea I value.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (1959) identified the effect, with Ehrenberg and Siday earlier. Bohm is deceased and absent from the list. Berry (1984) identified the geometric phase, with Pancharatnam as precursor and Aharonov-Anandan generalising it. Aharonov and Berry form a plausible pair, but the two discoveries are separate and a joint prize joins distinct contributions.
assessment.maturity: Both effects are confirmed in many experiments, such as Tonomura's electron holography and mesoscopic rings, and are standard textbook material. Recognition is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: The two discoveries are conceptually related but distinct, and a joint citation could look artificial.
Priority questions (Ehrenberg-Siday, Pancharatnam) and the deceased co-originator Bohm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and make precision tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a redefinition of the second feasible. The magic-wavelength idea is simple and general, and the effect on metrology is large.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice, and Ye's group built the best-performing clocks and drove their accuracy. Together they form a plausible pair. Hall and Hänsch have already been honoured for combs, and Ye's comb and cold-atom work is substantially his own.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across several groups and species, and active redefinition discussions. Mature, and probably timely.
uncertainties: Whether it is physics-prize significant or seen as an incremental step after previous clock and comb prizes.
Whether ion-clock work (Wineland, Rosenband) competes for the same recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire flat-band physics, with correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable system. The Bistritzer-MacDonald calculation gave a simple and surprisingly predictive mechanism for flat bands at a magic angle.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted the flat bands. Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators (2018) observed the correlated and superconducting states. Prediction and experiment give a natural configuration, though Cao and others in the experimental group, and Dean's and Yacoby's work, are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Strong replication and a huge follow-on literature, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and the correlated phases is still debated. Probably somewhat early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Reproducibility and sample dependence of the observed phases.
The role of earlier work on twisted-graphene band structure (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory with the principle of minimal frustration explains how proteins find their native folds despite a vast configuration space, using the statistical mechanics of disordered systems such as spin glasses and the random energy model. It is a clean theoretical idea with a physical mechanism and wide impact in biophysics.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes (1987) introduced the spin-glass analogy, and Onuchic and Wolynes developed the funnel picture with others. Other contributors such as Dill, Go and Thirumalai have claims, so attribution is only partially settled.
assessment.maturity: Supported by simulations, folding-kinetics experiments and coarse-grained models, but it is a conceptual framework and not a single measurement. Its status in the physics prize context is uncertain, and the field overlaps with chemistry.
uncertainties: Chemistry versus physics fit, particularly after the 2024 chemistry prize for protein structure prediction.
Priority and credit among competing folding theories.
Limited direct experimental test of the landscape picture.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of Hubbard-type models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and quantum gas microscopy, lets one engineer and observe strongly correlated many-body systems. It connects directly to statistical mechanics and condensed matter theory.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation. Greiner, Hansch and Bloch observed the Mott transition, and Bloch and Greiner developed quantum gas microscopes. Jaksch is outside the credited names and Cirac is an equally plausible theorist. Overlap with B031 complicates attribution, and Bose-Einstein condensation prizes (2001) have already recognised the underlying platform.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature experimentally. Fermionic Hubbard physics, such as the antiferromagnetic and pseudogap regime, is still an open goal, so the promise of solving the Hubbard model is not fully delivered.
uncertainties: Overlap with B031 on credited theorists, and the question of who is the decisive theorist.
Whether the quantum-simulation payoff for open condensed matter problems is yet sufficient.
